definition_en: the act or process of combining parts so that they form one whole
core_image: 几条小溪汇进同一条河道，原来的沙洲被水连成一片
scene: 小镇上原本分开的两条公交线合并成一条线路，站牌也换了。 The integration of the two schools took three careful years.
sceneCN: 这里 integration 是「整合、一体化」（第 1 个义项：把各部分合成整体的过程），句意为两所学校合并花了谨慎的三年。画面里的物件：合并站牌、新线路图、车票。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ion 构成，义为「整合；使一体」
由 integrate 加 -ed 构成，义为「一体化的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「瓦解」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「主张融合的」

senses.title: Putting parts into one system
senses.definition: the process of joining separate systems or parts so that they work as one
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的系统或部分接起来，使之作为一个整体运转的过程
senses.example: The integration of the ticketing and booking systems cut waiting lines in half.
senses.exampleCN: 售票与订票系统的整合让排队长龙减去一半。
senses.why: It is the noun of action of integrare, "to make whole".
senses.whyCN: 它是 integrare「使完整」这一动词的行为名词。

senses.title: People living together
senses.definition: the process by which different groups become full members of the same society
senses.definitionCN: 不同群体成为同一社会正式成员的过程
senses.example: Integration of newcomers works best when neighbours meet often.
senses.exampleCN: 新来者与邻居常来常往时，融合效果最好。
senses.why: The social sense grew after schools and workplaces were opened to everyone.
senses.whyCN: 社会义在学校与工作场所向所有人开放之后发展起来。

senses.title: Making markets and states one
senses.definition: the uniting of separate economies or regions into a single market or union
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的经济体或地区结成统一市场或联盟
senses.example: Economic integration made crossing the border a formality.
senses.exampleCN: 经济一体化让过境成了一道手续。
senses.why: Politicians took the word for treaties that bring neighbouring markets under one set of rules.
senses.whyCN: 政治家借这个词指把邻国市场纳入同一套规则的条约。

senses.title: In maths and science
senses.definition: the operation of adding up many small parts to get a total, or the total so found
senses.definitionCN: 把许多微小部分累加求得总量的运算，或由此求得的总量
senses.example: Learning integration comes after students master simple functions.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在掌握简单函数之后才学积分。
senses.why: Calculus uses the same metaphor: infinitely many thin strips sum to one whole area.
senses.whyCN: 微积分沿用同一比喻：无数细条累加成一块完整的面积。

intro.en: Integration is the Latin noun of action behind integrare; English borrowed it for both building and mathematics.
intro.cn: integration 是 integrare 背后的拉丁语行为名词，英语借来表达「整合」与数学上的「积分」。

items.en: Integer "whole, untouched" comes from in- "not" and a root meaning to touch.
items.cn: integer「完整的、未被触动的」来自 in-「不」与表示「触碰」的词根。

items.en: Integratio first named the restoring of a whole, including a person's health.
items.cn: integratio 最初指恢复完整，包括人的健康。

items.en: Seventeenth-century English used it for forming a whole out of parts.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语用它表示由部分构成整体。

items.en: Mathematicians then made it the name of summing small pieces into a total.
items.cn: 数学家随后让它成为把小块累加成总量的名称。

items.en: Modern social writing applies it to schools, nations, and migration.
items.cn: 现代的社会写作把它用于学校、国家与移民。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin whole; the near-meaning group names other ways of joining.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「完整」；近义组列其他「结合」的方式。

entries.definition: Honesty and wholeness of character.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正直；完整」，指品性。

entries.definition: The verb of joining into one whole.
A whole number in arithmetic.
Merging so completely that the parts lose their shape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「融合」，各部分完全失去原形。

entries.definition: A joining of groups, often formal or political.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「联合」，多指正式或政治上的结合。

entries.definition: The combining of two companies into one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合并」，多指两家公司合成一家。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the whole-number root and the places where integration is actually discussed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子沿着「完整」这一词根走，并附着在以 integration 为话题的场合上。

normal.en: Integer means whole: integration is the making of that whole.
normal.cn: integer 意为整：integration 就是把这个整做出来的过程。

normal.en: Bus routes, schools, and banks all talk about integration.
normal.cn: 公交线路、学校、银行都在谈整合。

normal.en: Economic integration means one market with one rulebook.
normal.cn: 经济一体化意味着一个市场、一套规则。

normal.en: Social integration needs friendship, not just laws.
normal.cn: 社会融合需要友谊，而不只是法律。

normal.en: Add up many small pieces and you get an integral.
normal.cn: 把许多小块累加，就得到一个积分。

abstract.en: Integration is the moment seams stop being visible.
abstract.cn: 整合就是接缝不再被人看见的那一刻。

abstract.en: A city is an integration of strangers into neighbours.
abstract.cn: 城市是把陌生人融合成邻居的过程。

abstract.en: Every whole is a promise that the pieces will stay together.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都是一份「各部分不散」的承诺。

examples.en: Integration of the two payroll systems saved a week of work each month.
examples.cn: 两套工资系统的整合每月省下一周的工作量。

examples.en: The city funds language classes to support broader integration.
examples.cn: 市政出资办语言班，以支持更广泛的融合。

examples.en: Full integration into the group takes most new members a term.
examples.cn: 大多数新成员要一个学期才能完全融入群体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因太鬼雷神」——零件太奇特，靠雷神一把合成整体

root: 拉丁语 tangere「触碰」→ integer「完整的」（in-「不」+ 触碰）→ integrare「使完整」→ integratio「更新、使完整」→ 英语 integration。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: joining systems, bringing people together, uniting markets, and summing small parts in maths.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：整合系统、让群体融合、联合市场，以及数学上的求和积分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small streams flow into one river and the sand bars disappear.
core.cn: 核心意象：小溪汇入大河，原来的沙洲消失。

branches.en: THE BUS MAP: two routes become one line.
branches.cn: 公交图这条线：两条线路变成一条。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM: newcomers become ordinary neighbours.
branches.cn: 教室这条线：新来者变成平常的邻居。

branches.en: THE BORDER: markets merge under shared rules.
branches.cn: 边境这条线：市场在共同规则下合并。

branches.en: THE STRIPS: countless thin pieces add up to a whole area.
branches.cn: 细条这条线：无数细条累加成一整块面积。

branches.en: THE LINK: systems and people are both made whole by being joined.
branches.cn: 连接线：系统与人都是因被连接而变得完整。

intro.en: Integration = in- "not" + teg- "touch" + -ration, the noun ending -ation on the whole stem.
intro.cn: integration = in-「不」+ teg-「触碰」+ -ation，名词词尾加在整个词干上。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer, integrare and integratio are attested in classical texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer、integrare、integratio 在古典文献中均有记载。

items.exampleCN: 它给出「未被触动」的性质。

items.example: Also seen in intact and contact.
items.exampleCN: 也见于 intact 与 contact。

items.example: Whole numbers still carry the name.
It forms the noun of action.

items.exampleCN: 在 disintegration 中表示相反。

items.example: The reverse process has its own name.
items.exampleCN: 相反的过程有自己的名字。

definition_zh: 生物；有机体；生物体；（社会或组织的）有机整体
definition_en: an individual living thing, or a whole whose parts work together like those of a living body
core_image: 一个由许多器官协同工作的完整生命体，每个部件都为整体服务
scene: 一只小小的生物体内，细胞数量可能比这座城市的人口还多。 A single organism can contain more cells than there are people in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 organism 指「生物」（第 1 个义项：独立存活的个体生命）；句意：一个生物体内的细胞数可能超过这座城市的人口。图中可辨识物件：示意的细胞群、器官剖面、放大镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 生物；有机体；生物体；（比喻）有机整体、组织体

derivatives.zh: 有机的；生物的；有机农业的
生物个体的；个体层面的

senses.title: An Individual Living Thing
senses.definition: a single living thing, such as an animal, plant or bacterium
senses.definitionCN: 单个活物，如动物、植物或细菌
senses.example: A single organism can contain more cells than there are people in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 一个生物体内的细胞数可能超过这座城市的人口。
senses.why: Greek organon meant 'tool, instrument'. An organism is a body whose parts work as instruments for the whole, which is why the word stresses organized cooperation rather than mere life.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 organon 意为「工具、器具」；organism 是各部件作为整体之工具而协同工作的身体，因此这个词强调有组织的协作，而不只是「活着」。

senses.title: Microscopic Life
senses.titleCN: 微生物：肉眼难见的个体
senses.definition: a microscopic living thing, especially a bacterium or fungus
senses.definitionCN: 微小的活物，尤指细菌或真菌
senses.example: The water contained several harmful organisms.
senses.exampleCN: 水中含有几种有害微生物。
senses.why: In hygiene and medicine the word usually points to things too small to see. The size is not part of the definition, but the context supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 在卫生与医学语境里，这个词通常指小到看不见的东西；大小并不属于定义，而是由语境补上的。

senses.title: A Social Whole
senses.titleCN: 有机整体：社会或组织的比喻
senses.definition: a society or organization treated as a body whose parts depend on one another
senses.definitionCN: 被看作相互依存之身体的社会或组织
senses.example: Some nineteenth-century writers called society a living organism.
senses.exampleCN: 一些十九世纪的作家把社会称为活的有机体。
senses.why: The metaphor claims that institutions are not assembled machines but growing bodies. It has been used both to justify reform and to argue that parts cannot be replaced at will.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻主张制度不是拼装的机器，而是生长出来的身体；它既被用来支持改革，也被用来论证各部分不能随意替换。

senses.title: Engineered Life
senses.titleCN: 改造过的生物：转基因个体
senses.definition: a living thing whose genetic material has been deliberately altered
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质被人为改动的活物
senses.example: Regulations cover any genetically modified organism sold as food.
senses.exampleCN: 法规涵盖任何作为食品出售的转基因生物。
senses.why: Modern biotechnology made the word a legal category. The organism is still an individual living thing; only its genes have been edited, which is why the modifier carries the weight.
senses.whyCN: 现代生物技术把这个词变成法律类别；该生物仍是独立活物，只是基因被编辑过，因此分量落在修饰语上。

senses.title: Model Organism
senses.titleCN: 模式生物：用于研究的代表
senses.definition: a species studied in the laboratory to understand general biological processes
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室中研究、以理解一般生物过程的物种
senses.example: The fruit fly became the model organism for genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 果蝇成了遗传学的模式生物。
senses.why: Research needs a stand-in that is easy to keep and well understood. The word marks the individual, while the phrase marks its representative role.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要一个易饲养、已被充分理解的替身；这个词标出的是个体，而短语标出的是它的代表角色。

senses.title: An Ecological Unit
senses.titleCN: 生态个体：生态学中的计数单位
senses.definition: an individual counted as a unit in an ecological study
senses.definitionCN: 生态研究中作为一个单位来计数的个体
senses.example: The survey counted every organism larger than a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查统计了每一个大于一毫米的生物个体。
senses.why: Ecology counts individuals to estimate populations. Here the word is almost a unit of measurement, defined by the size cut-off the researcher chooses.
senses.whyCN: 生态学通过数个体来估计种群；此时这个词几乎是一个计量单位，其边界由研究者选定的尺寸下限决定。

senses.title: An Organized Whole
senses.titleCN: 有机整体：哲学意义上的整体
senses.definition: a whole whose parts are mutually dependent and cannot be understood alone
senses.definitionCN: 各部分相互依赖、不能孤立理解的整体
senses.example: For the philosopher, the mind is an organism, not a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 在这位哲学家看来，心灵是有机整体，而不是机器。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the word against mechanism. If parts only make sense in the whole, explanation must begin with the whole, not with the smallest piece.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用这个词来反对机械论：如果部件只有在整体中才有意义，解释就必须从整体开始，而不是从最小零件开始。

senses.title: A Working Body
senses.titleCN: 运作中的组织体：机构如身体
senses.definition: an organization understood through the cooperation of its parts
senses.definitionCN: 通过各部分协作来理解的机构
senses.example: The department behaves like an organism with its own metabolism.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部门像一个有自己的代谢方式的有机体那样运作。
senses.why: Management writing borrows the biological image to talk about flow, feedback and adaptation. The claim is that removing one part changes the health of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 管理写作借生物学意象来谈流动、反馈与适应；其主张是：拿掉一个部件会改变其余部分的健康。

intro.en: Organism is a modern formation on Greek organon 'tool, instrument, organ', from ergon 'work'. It was coined in the nineteenth century; the exact coiner and first date are uncertain.
intro.cn: organism 是建立在希腊 organon「工具、器具、器官」之上的近代构词，而 organon 出自 ergon「工作」。该词于十九世纪被造出；确切的造词者与首见年代不确定。

items.en: Ergon meant 'work, deed'. Its Indo-European root also gives English work and the Greek adjective energetikos, source of energy.
items.cn: ergon 意为「工作、行动」，其印欧词根也给出英语 work，以及希腊形容词 energetikos——energy 的来源。

items.en: Organon meant 'a tool or instrument', and by extension an organ of the body, since an organ is the body's instrument for a task. Aristotle's logical works were called the Organon, the tool of reasoning.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，引申指身体器官，因为器官就是身体完成某项任务的工具。亚里士多德的逻辑著作被称为 Organon，即推理的工具。

items.en: Latin organum kept the senses of instrument and, later, musical instrument and body organ. English organ and organize descend from this line.
items.cn: 拉丁 organum 保留「器具」义，后来又指乐器与身体器官；英语 organ 与 organize 都出自这条线索。

items.en: Organism was formed in the nineteenth century to name a living body as an organized whole. The exact coiner is uncertain; the word spread with biology and with the philosophy of organized wholes.
items.cn: organism 于十九世纪被造出，用来指作为有组织整体的活体。确切的造词者不确定；该词随生物学以及「有组织整体」的哲学而传播开来。

items.en: Social thinkers soon applied organism to societies and institutions. The metaphor was attractive because it explained interdependence, but it was also criticized for making change seem like mere growth.
items.cn: 社会思想家很快把 organism 用于社会与机构。这个比喻之所以有吸引力，是因为它能解释相互依存；但它也因让变革显得只是「生长」而受到批评。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective relatives and from organization. The second holds near-synonyms that name life at different scales.
note.cn: 第一组区分该名词与其形容词亲属以及 organization；第二组是不同尺度上指称生命的近义词。

entries.definition: Means 'of living things' or 'grown without chemicals'. It describes a quality, while organism names the living individual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「生物的」或「不用化学方式种植的」；它描述性质，而 organism 命名的是活的个体。

entries.definition: A structured group such as a company, or the act of arranging. It shares the organ root but names arrangement, not life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指公司一类有结构的人群，或安排的动作；它同出 organ 词根，但命名的是安排，而不是生命。

entries.definition: A body part with a specific function, or a musical instrument. It is the instrument that the organism as a whole uses.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指有特定功能的身体部件，或指乐器；它是整个 organism 所使用的「工具」。

entries.definition: A living being, especially an animal. It is warmer and less technical than organism.
entries.definitionCN: 活物，尤指动物；比 organism 更有温度，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: A living entity, or existence itself. It is broader and vaguer, often used where organism would sound clinical.
entries.definitionCN: 活的存在者，或存在本身；更宽泛、更模糊，在 organism 显得过于临床的地方常用它。

entries.definition: A microscopic living thing. It is narrower than organism, which covers elephants as well as bacteria.
entries.definitionCN: 微小的活物；比 organism 狭窄，因为后者同样包括大象与细菌。

entries.definition: Any kind of living thing, often used when imagining life elsewhere. It stresses kind rather than individual.
entries.definitionCN: 任何种类的活物，常用于设想别处的生命；强调种类而非个体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: organon 'tool' + -ism: a body whose organs are tools for the whole.
normal.cn: organon「工具」+ -ism：器官作为整体工具的身体。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organic, organism, organismal, organismic, organize, organization, organelle.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organic、organism、organismal、organismic、organize、organization、organelle。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: living organism, model organism, single-celled organism, genetically modified organism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：生物、模式生物、单细胞生物、转基因生物。

normal.en: organism is the living thing; organization is the arranged group.
normal.cn: organism 是活的东西，organization 是安排成的群体。

normal.en: organic describes a quality; organism names the individual.
normal.cn: organic 描述性质，organism 命名个体。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every tool has its place and every worker serves the same finished object.
abstract.cn: 想象一间作坊，每件工具都有位置，每个工人服务于同一件成品。

abstract.en: Picture a city that repairs its own roads without anyone giving the order.
abstract.cn: 想象一座自己修补道路、无需谁下命令的城市。

abstract.en: Picture a watch that grows new wheels instead of replacing them.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表会自己长出新的齿轮，而不是更换齿轮。

examples.en: No organism can survive without water for long.
examples.cn: 没有生物能在缺水的情况下长期存活。

examples.en: The pond supports thousands of microscopic organisms.
examples.cn: 这个池塘养育着数以千计的微小生物。

examples.en: The model organism is chosen because its genome is small.
examples.cn: 选择该模式生物，是因为它的基因组很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: organ（器官）+ ism（体系、状态）→ 由器官协同构成的整体 → 生物、有机体

root: 希腊 ergon「工作」→ organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organum → 英语 organ → 十九世纪加 -ism 构成 organism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all concern an organized living whole: an individual, a microbe, a society, an engineered plant or animal, a laboratory model, an ecological unit, a philosophical whole and a working institution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都涉及有组织的活的整体：个体、微生物、社会、被改造的动植物、实验室模型、生态单位、哲学整体与运作中的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many organs working as one body, each part serving the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多器官作为一个身体协同工作，每个部件都为整体服务。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL UNIT: from a whale to a bacterium, one living thing counted as one.
branches.cn: 个体单位：从鲸到细菌，一个活物算作一个。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE MAJORITY: hygiene and medicine use the word for life too small to see.
branches.cn: 看不见的多数：卫生与医学用这个词指小到看不见的生命。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL METAPHOR: societies and departments are described as bodies whose parts depend on each other.
branches.cn: 社会比喻：社会与部门被描述为部件相互依存的身体。

branches.en: LIFE UNDER DESIGN: engineered organisms and model organisms exist because humans chose and altered them.
branches.cn: 被设计过的生命：转基因生物与模式生物之所以存在，是因为人选择并改动了它们。

branches.en: THE PHILOSOPHICAL WHOLE: against mechanism, the whole explains the parts rather than the reverse.
branches.cn: 哲学整体：与机械论相对，整体解释部件，而不是反过来。

intro.en: Organism is a Greek-derived root with the English suffix -ism: an instrument-root, a suffix of system or state, and later a biological noun.
intro.cn: organism 是希腊来源的词根加英语后缀 -ism：表示器具的词根、表示体系或状态的后缀，后来成为生物学名词。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon reached Latin as organum and produced organ, organic, organism, organize, organization and organelle. The root ergon also underlies energy.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 以拉丁 organum 进入拉丁语，衍生 organ、organic、organism、organize、organization、organelle；词根 ergon 也支撑 energy。

items.example: The organism responds to light within seconds.
items.exampleCN: 该生物在数秒内就对光作出反应。

items.meaning: of living things; grown without chemicals
items.meaningCN: 生物的；不用化学方式种植的
items.example: Organic matter in the soil feeds the crop.
items.exampleCN: 土壤中的有机物滋养作物。

items.meaning: at the level of the individual organism
items.example: Organismal responses differ from cellular ones.
items.exampleCN: 个体层面的反应不同于细胞层面的反应。

items.meaning: treating the whole as an organized body
items.example: Organismic biology studies wholes, not only parts.
items.exampleCN: 有机体生物学研究整体，而不只是部件。

items.meaning: a body part with a task
items.meaningCN: 承担某项任务的身体部件
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.meaning: a small structure inside a cell
to arrange parts into a working whole
items.meaningCN: 把部件安排成可运作的整体
items.example: She organized the files by year.

items.meaning: an arranged group or the act of arranging
items.meaningCN: 安排成的群体或安排的行为

latinEntries.structure: Greek ergon (work); root also in Latin energia

definition_zh: 执行；实施；处决；演奏；表演
definition_en: to carry out a plan or order, to put someone to death by law, or to perform skillfully
core_image: 沿着标记路线跑到终点的跑者
scene: 团队按计划执行了新方案。 The team executed the new plan without delay.
sceneCN: 这里 execute 是「执行、实施」（第 1 个义项）；句意：团队按计划执行了新方案。

senses.title: Carry out
senses.definition: to carry out a plan, order, or piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 把计划、命令或工作付诸实施
senses.example: The crew executed the rescue plan perfectly.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队完美地执行了救援计划。
senses.why: The task is followed all the way to its end.
senses.whyCN: 任务被一路跟随到终点。

senses.title: Put to death
senses.definition: to kill someone as a legal punishment
senses.definitionCN: 作为法律惩罚将某人处死
senses.example: The prisoner was executed at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯在黎明时被处决。
senses.why: The sentence is carried out to its final end.
senses.whyCN: 判决被一路执行到最终结局。

senses.title: Perform
senses.definition: to perform a difficult piece of music or movement
senses.definitionCN: 演奏难度较高的音乐段落或完成动作
senses.example: She executed the final turn with grace.
senses.exampleCN: 她优雅地完成了最后的转身动作。
senses.why: The performer follows the score through without a break.
senses.whyCN: 表演者不间断地跟随乐谱走完。

intro.en: Execute comes from Latin exsequi, to follow through.
intro.cn: execute 源自拉丁语 exsequi，意为跟随到底。

items.en: Sequi means to follow.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随。

items.en: Exsequi joins ex-, out, with sequi, to follow.
items.cn: exsequi 由 ex-（出）与 sequi（跟随）组成。

items.en: Exsequi means to follow a task to the end.
items.cn: exsequi 意为把任务跟到终点。

items.en: Old French executer carries out the sense of carrying through.
items.cn: 古法语 executer 保留贯彻到底之意。

items.en: English execute adds the sense of legal killing.
items.cn: 英语 execute 增加了依法处死之义。

note.en: Execute follows a task through; perform shows it to others.
note.cn: execute 强调把任务贯彻到底，perform 强调展示给他人看。

entries.definition: the carrying out of a plan or sentence
a senior manager
a person who carries out a will
to do what was planned
to put a decision into practice
to do a task or show a skill

normalIntro.en: Execute follows a task until it is done.
normalIntro.cn: execute 跟随任务一直做到完。

normal.en: The team executed the plan on time.
normal.cn: 团队按时执行了计划。

normal.en: Soldiers must execute an order at once.
normal.cn: 士兵必须立即执行命令。

normal.en: The software executes the program in seconds.
normal.cn: 软件在几秒内运行完程序。

normal.en: The court executed the sentence at dawn.
normal.cn: 法庭在黎明执行了判决。

normal.en: She executed the dance with precision.
normal.cn: 她精准地完成了这支舞。

abstract.en: Picture a runner following a route to the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者沿路线跑到终点。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand signing a page and finishing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手签完一页并把它完成。

abstract.en: Think of a machine that turns an order into action.
abstract.cn: 想象一台把命令变成行动的机器。

examples.en: They executed the evacuation without a single mistake.
examples.cn: 他们执行撤离时没有出一次错。

examples.en: The pianist executed the passage at great speed.
examples.cn: 钢琴家以极快速度演奏了这一段。

examples.en: He was executed for treason in the old story.
examples.cn: 在那个古老故事里，他因叛国罪被处决。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ ecute（跟随）」——一路跟着把事情做出来，就是执行；跟到终点也可能是处决。

root: 拉丁语 exsequi（跟随到底）＝ ex-（出）＋ sequi（跟随）→ execute，核心义「跟着把事情做到底」。

sensesIntro.en: Execute means to carry out a task, to put someone to death by law, or to perform a movement or piece.
sensesIntro.cn: execute 意为执行任务、依法处死某人，或完成动作与演奏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner following a marked route.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿着标记路线奔跑的人。

branches.en: Carrying out a task is the central sense.
branches.cn: 执行任务是中心义项。

branches.en: The legal sense ends a life.
branches.cn: 法律义项终结一条生命。

branches.en: Performers execute difficult passages.
branches.cn: 表演者完成高难度段落。

branches.en: Both senses carry a task to its end.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把任务推进到终点。

branches.en: Both show skill in completing something.
branches.cn: 两者都体现完成某事的技术。

intro.en: Execute combines ex-, out, with Latin sequi, to follow.
intro.cn: execute 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 sequi（跟随）组成。

latinIntro.en: Exsequi gives French executer and then English execute.
latinIntro.cn: exsequi 给出法语 executer，再到英语 execute。

items.exampleCN: sequi 出现在 sequence 中。
executive 标记行使职权的一方。

items.meaning: one who carries out a will
items.exampleCN: executor 加上了表示人的词尾。

latinEntries.example: Exsequi is the source of execute.
latinEntries.exampleCN: exsequi 是 execute 的来源。

definition_en: the process of gradually collecting something, or the amount collected
core_image: 仓库角落里的箱子一年年往上码
scene: 机翼上的冰越结越厚，飞行员开始担心。 The accumulation of ice on the wings worried the pilot.
sceneCN: 这里的 accumulation 是「堆积过程」（第 1 个义项：逐渐积聚起来）；句意是机翼结冰让飞行员担心。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「积累；堆积」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「累积的」
由词干加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「蓄能器」

senses.title: The process of building up
senses.definition: the gradual process by which something increases in amount
senses.definitionCN: 某物数量逐渐增多的过程
senses.example: The accumulation of data took several years.
senses.exampleCN: 数据的积累花了几年时间。
senses.why: The noun ending turns the act of heaping into a process, so the word names the slow adding rather than the heap itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾把「堆」这个动作变作过程，所以这个词指的是慢慢添加的过程，而不是堆本身。

senses.title: A mass that has piled up
senses.definition: an amount of something that has gathered into a mass
senses.definitionCN: 已经聚成一团或一层的一定量东西
senses.example: An accumulation of leaves blocked the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 积起来的落叶堵住了排水口。
senses.why: Once the process stops, what is left is a visible mass; English uses the same noun for the result and the activity.
senses.whyCN: 过程一停，留下的就是看得见的一团；英语用同一个名词兼指动作与结果。

intro.en: The noun is the Latin action noun built on the verb for heaping.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁语中由「堆」的动词构成的动作名词。

items.en: cumulus named a heap or a rounded mass.
items.cn: cumulus 指堆或圆团。

items.en: accumulare meant to heap something up.
items.cn: accumulare 意为把东西堆起来。

items.en: accumulatio named the act of heaping.
items.cn: accumulatio 指「堆叠」这一行为。

items.en: accumulation entered English as a scholarly noun of increase.
items.cn: accumulation 在十六世纪进入英语，是书面语中表示「增多」的名词。

items.en: it now appears in finance, science and everyday talk of clutter.
items.cn: 如今它出现在金融、科学以及日常谈杂物堆积的场合。

note.en: The first group shares the heap root; the second names other kinds of increase.
note.cn: 第一组共享「堆」的词根；第二组是别的表示增多的说法。

entries.definition: to heap something up over time
growing by repeated addition
something that stores what is added
added up over successive steps
a gradual increase or gathering
a group of things brought together
a heap of objects resting on one another
a supply stored up for future use

normalIntro.en: Everything here hangs on the Latin heap cumulus.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条都挂在拉丁语的「堆」cumulus 上。

normal.en: cumulus is the heap, and -ation turns heaping into a process.
normal.cn: cumulus 是「堆」，-ation 把「堆」变成过程。

normal.en: the same noun serves both the act and the pile left behind.
normal.cn: 同一个名词既指动作，也指留下来的那堆东西。

normal.en: capital accumulation is a fixed phrase in economics.
normal.cn: capital accumulation 是经济学里的固定说法。

normal.en: dust accumulation is the everyday version of the same idea.
normal.cn: dust accumulation 是同一想法在日常里的版本。

normal.en: the plural accumulations usually points to several separate piles.
normal.cn: 复数 accumulations 通常指分开的几堆。

abstract.en: See boxes stacked higher in a warehouse corner each year.
abstract.cn: 想象仓库角落的箱子一年比一年码得高。

abstract.en: Picture a layer of ice thickening on a wing.
abstract.cn: 想象机翼上的冰层一点点变厚。

abstract.en: Think of a bank statement where interest keeps adding to the balance.
abstract.cn: 想象银行账单上利息不断并进余额。

examples.en: The accumulation of evidence finally convinced the judge.
examples.cn: 证据的不断累积最终说服了法官。

examples.en: An accumulation of sand had blocked the road.
examples.cn: 堆积的沙子堵住了道路。

examples.en: Slow accumulation of skills made him a fine craftsman.
examples.cn: 技艺的慢慢积累使他成了好工匠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿丘缪累身」——阿丘把东西越堆越多，最后累到自己身上。

root: 拉丁语 accumulatio，源自 accumulare（堆起来），词根 cumulus 意为「堆」；本义是堆叠的动作，后指积累的过程与积成之物。

sensesIntro.en: The noun looks at the heap from two sides: the slow adding, and the mass that remains.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从两面看同一堆东西：慢慢添加的过程，以及最后留下的那团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pile still growing, then standing finished.
core.cn: 核心意象：一边还在长高、一边已经成形的堆。

branches.en: the slow adding of data, capital or skill
branches.cn: 数据、资本或技艺的缓慢添加

branches.en: the visible heap of leaves, sand or ice
branches.cn: 看得见的落叶、沙子或冰层

branches.en: an action that leaves a tangible result
branches.cn: 留下实物的那个动作

branches.en: time as the quiet agent of increase
branches.cn: 时间作为无声的增长者

branches.en: quantity you can measure and clear away
branches.cn: 可以丈量、也可以清走的数量

intro.en: A Latin verb stem plus a noun ending carries the whole idea of heaping.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁动词词干加一个名词词尾，就承载了「堆」的全部意思。

latinIntro.en: cumulus, the heap, is also the root of cumulative and of the cloud name.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「堆」的 cumulus 也是 cumulative 和云名 cumulus 的词根。

definition_zh: 通知；告知；申报；报备；推送通知
definition_en: to tell someone something officially, especially in writing, and to report a fact to an authority
core_image: 一封封好的信，被递到那个必须知道的人手里
scene: 护照到期之前，窗口里的工作人员把一封打印好的信推到申请人面前，请他核对地址后签字。 The bank notified every customer of the new fee in writing.
sceneCN: 这里 notify 是「正式通知、告知」（第 1 个义项：把消息正式送到某人手里）；句意为银行用书面形式把新收费告知每位客户。图中可辨识物件：办事窗口、打印的信、签字笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 notify 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「通知；通告」
由 notify 加表「做某事的人或物」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「通知者；通知程序」
由 notify 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「须上报的」

senses.title: To tell someone something officially
senses.definition: to give someone information in an official or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 以官方或正式的方式把消息告诉某人
senses.example: Please notify us of any change in your contact details.
senses.exampleCN: 联系方式若有变动，请通知我们。
senses.why: Notus means known and -ify means to make, so notify is literally to make something known; its force sits on the telling, not on the seeing.
senses.whyCN: notus 意为「已知的」，-ify 意为「使」，所以 notify 字面就是「使某事被知道」；它的着力点在「告诉」，而不在「看见」。

senses.title: To report a fact to an authority
senses.definition: to report something to an official body because a rule requires it
senses.definitionCN: 因规定要求而把事情报告给官方机构
senses.example: All new cases must be notified to the health department.
senses.exampleCN: 所有新病例都必须上报卫生部门。
senses.why: The same making-known turns into a duty when a rule demands it, so the verb picks up the legal sense of filing a report with an office.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「使被知道」，一旦有规定要求，就变成一种义务，动词于是添上「向机关报备」的法律含义。

senses.title: Of software, to send a message to a user
senses.definition: to have a program send a message that appears on a user's screen
senses.definitionCN: 由程序发出消息，显示在用户屏幕上
senses.example: The app notifies you when your train is delayed.
senses.exampleCN: 列车晚点时，这款应用会推送提醒。
senses.why: A machine now does the telling, so the verb extends from people to software that makes a message known on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 如今由机器来完成告知，动词便从人扩展到软件：把一条消息呈现在屏幕上让人知道。

intro.en: Notify is a Latin compound meaning to make known: a participle for known joined to a verb of making, carried into English through French.
intro.cn: notify 是一个意为「使被知道」的拉丁语复合词：表示「已知」的分词接上一个表示「制作」的动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Noscere, to get to know, supplied the family with its participle notus, meaning known.
items.cn: noscere 意为认识，为这个词族提供了分词 notus，意为「已知的」。

items.en: Facere meant to make or to do, and it supplied the -ficare ending used in verbs of making.
items.cn: facere 意为制作、做，提供了动词中常见的词尾 -ficare。

items.en: Medieval Latin joined the two into notificare, to make known, a word at home in documents and official acts.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把两者合成 notificare，意为「使被知道」，是文书与官方行为里的常用词。

items.en: Old French notifier carried that official flavour into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 notifier 带着这份官方色彩，在诺曼时期之后进入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the official tone, adds the legal sense of reporting to authorities, and now lets software notify its users.
items.cn: 现代英语保留官方语气，添上向主管部门报备的法律义，如今又让软件向用户推送通知。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family derived from this verb; the near-meaning group collects verbs for passing information.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个动词派生的同族词；近义组收表示传递信息的动词。

entries.definition: A message that officially tells someone something.
entries.definitionCN: 正式告知某人的一条消息。

entries.definition: A person or program that sends a notification.
Required by law to be reported to an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 法律规定必须向主管部门报告的。

entries.definition: To tell someone facts they did not have.
entries.definitionCN: 把对方尚不知道的事实告知。

entries.definition: To warn someone about something urgent.
To make something public to many people at once.
To give information to someone in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 用言语把信息告诉某人。

normalIntro.en: The verb is a Latin sum of known plus make, so every use of it contains someone who must be told and something that must become known.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词是拉丁语的「已知」加「使」，所以它每次出现，都含着一个必须被告诉的人和一桩必须被知道的事。

normal.en: Notus means known and -ify means to make, so notify is to make known, which is why it always needs someone to receive the message.
normal.cn: notus 意为已知，-ify 意为使，所以 notify 就是「使被知道」；也正因如此，它总需要一个收消息的人。

normal.en: The frame notify someone of something is standard, with of marking what the message is about.
normal.cn: notify someone of something 是标准句式，of 后面标出消息的内容。

normal.en: Notice comes from the noun notitia and centres on seeing; notify comes from notificare and centres on telling. A glance notices, an office notifies.
normal.cn: notice 出自名词 notitia，重心在看见；notify 出自 notificare，重心在告知。眼睛可以 notice，机关则要 notify。

normal.en: Notification adds -ation to the verb, naming the message that arrives rather than the act of sending it.
normal.cn: notification 在动词后加 -ation，指送达的那条消息，而不是发送这个动作。

normal.en: In law notifiable diseases must be reported, so the adjective carries an obligation that the verb alone does not.
normal.cn: 在法律里 notifiable disease 必须上报，这个形容词带着动词本身所没有的义务。

abstract.en: Notice is what your eyes do; notify is what an office does with a stamp.
abstract.cn: notice 是眼睛做的事；notify 是机构盖章做的事。

abstract.en: Every notification is a small claim that someone out there needs to know.
abstract.cn: 每一条通知都是一个轻微的断言：外面有人需要知道这件事。

abstract.en: A word that once meant simply making known now runs through paper letters and phone screens without changing its core.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经只表示「使被知道」的词，如今穿行于纸质信件与手机屏幕，核心却没有变。

examples.en: The bank notified every customer of the new fee.
examples.cn: 银行把新收费告知了每位客户。

examples.en: You must notify the authorities within ten days of moving.
examples.cn: 搬家后十天之内必须向主管部门报备。

examples.en: The app notifies you when your train is delayed.
examples.cn: 列车晚点时，这款应用会推送提醒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺替饭」——答应替人把饭送到，还得正式通知一声；notify 就是通知。

root: notus（已知）+ -ify（使），经中世纪拉丁语 notificare、古法语 notifier 进入英语；与 notice 同源，但一个重在「看见」，一个重在「告知」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is making something known to a person who must act on it; the senses then divide by channel, from an ordinary official telling to a required report and to a message pushed by software.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把某事让一个必须据此行动的人知道；义项随后按渠道分开，从普通的正式告知，到规定要求的报备，再到软件推送的消息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed letter handed straight to the person who must know.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封封好的信，直接递到那个必须知道的人手里。

branches.en: a letter that reaches a customer before the fee changes
branches.cn: 收费变更前送到客户手里的信

branches.en: a clerk reading a name aloud from a list
branches.cn: 工作人员照着名单念出一个名字

branches.en: a form filed with a health office
branches.cn: 递交给卫生部门的一张表格

branches.en: a phone lighting up with a delay warning
branches.cn: 手机亮起的晚点提醒

branches.en: the same telling done first by a person, then by software
branches.cn: 同一件告知，先由人做，后由软件做

intro.en: The verb is Latin for making known: a participle for known plus a verb ending for making, and French changed the sound but not the sense.

definition_en: a country's warships taken as a fighting force; the armed service that operates them; a very dark blue colour
core_image: 一排灰色军舰贴着码头停靠，桅杆上的旗在雾里慢慢升起
scene: 港口清晨起了雾，一排灰色军舰贴着码头停靠，桅杆上的旗还没升起。 The navy kept the harbour closed until the fog lifted.
sceneCN: 这里是「海军舰队」（第 1 个义项：一国用于海上作战的舰船力量）；句意为雾散之前海军一直封锁着港口。图中可辨识物件：军舰、码头、雾、旗杆。

senses.title: A country's warships as a fighting fleet
senses.titleCN: 海军舰队；一国的战舰力量
senses.definition: the warships of a country, considered together as a force that fights at sea
senses.definitionCN: 把一国的军舰作为一个整体来看，即用于海上作战的力量
senses.example: The navy sent two ships to guard the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 海军派出两艘军舰去守卫海峡。
senses.why: Latin navis meant ship, and Old French turned it into navie, a collective word for a body of ships; the English word still starts from the picture of many hulls moving together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 navis 意为船，古法语把它变成 navie，指成队的船；英语这个词的起点仍是许多船体一起移动的画面。

senses.title: The naval service as a branch of the armed forces
senses.definition: the organization, ships and people that a state maintains to fight at sea, one of its armed services
senses.definitionCN: 国家为海上作战而维持的机构、舰船与人员，是军种之一
senses.example: He joined the navy at eighteen and served for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 他十八岁参加海军，服役十年。
senses.why: Once a fleet belongs to a state, it needs bases, ranks, pay and training; the name of the ships then passes to the institution that keeps them.
senses.whyCN: 当一支船队归国家所有，就需要基地、军衔、薪饷与训练；于是「船」的名字转而指维持这些船的机构。

senses.title: A very dark blue colour
senses.definition: a blue so dark that it looks almost black, used for uniforms and formal clothing
senses.definitionCN: 深到近乎黑色的蓝色，常用于制服与正式服装
senses.example: The curtains were a deep navy that made the room feel calm.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘是深沉的藏青色，让房间显得安静。
senses.why: Indigo dye held its colour in salt water, so naval cloth kept a depth that ordinary blue did not; when people needed a name for that particular dark blue, the uniform supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 靛蓝染料在海水里不易褪色，海军布料因此保住了寻常蓝色没有的深度；人们要给这种特定的深蓝起名时，制服就提供了一个现成的说法。

senses.title: Clothing in that dark blue shade
senses.definition: used of clothes, especially a dark blue that reads as almost black
senses.definitionCN: 用于衣物，尤指看起来近乎黑色的深蓝
senses.example: He wore a navy suit and a plain white shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿一套深蓝西装，配一件素白衬衫。
senses.why: Naval officers were long dressed in indigo cloth because the dye wore well at sea, so the colour of the uniform became a word for the colour itself, and then for clothes cut in it.
senses.whyCN: 海军军官长期穿靛蓝布料，因为这种染料在海上耐晒耐洗；制服的颜色于是成了颜色本身的名称，又进一步指用这种颜色做的衣服。

intro.en: Navy began as a French collective noun for a body of ships and only later attached itself to the warships of a state and to the colour of their cloth.
intro.cn: navy 最初是法语中表示「一队船」的集合名词，后来才附着到国家的战舰，以及战舰布料的那种颜色上。

items.en: Navis was the ordinary Latin word for a ship, and it stands behind naval, navigate and navy alike.
items.cn: navis 是拉丁语中表示「船」的常用词，naval、navigate 与 navy 都站在它后面。

items.en: Old French formed navie as a collective noun for a fleet, adding a group ending to the Latin stem for ship.
items.cn: 古法语用拉丁语「船」的词干加集合名词词尾，造出 navie，指一支船队。

items.en: Middle English borrowed navie as navy, still meaning a body of ships, whether for trade or for war.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 navie 写作 navy，仍指成队的船，商业与作战都可用。

items.en: With standing fleets and permanent admiralties, navy narrowed to the warships of the state, and naval uniforms gave the word a colour sense.
items.cn: 随着常备舰队与常设海军部出现，navy 收窄为国家战舰；海军制服又赋予这个词一层颜色义。

items.en: Modern English keeps the service, the fleet and the dark blue, and uses the adjective for suits and knitwear as readily as for warships.
items.cn: 现代英语保留军种、舰队与深蓝三义，形容词既可形容军舰，也可随口形容西装与针织衫。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words on the Latin stem for ship, including the adjective and the verb of sailing; the near-meaning group holds names for fleets and for the ships inside them.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「船」词干上的词，包括形容词与航行的动词；近义组收船队以及船队中各种船的名称。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin ship stem wearing a French collective ending, and its relatives all keep the image of hulls on water.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「船」的词干披上法语的集合词尾，它的同族词都保留着水上船体的画面。

normal.en: Latin navis meant ship, so navy began as a crowd of ships rather than as an institution.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 navis 意为船，所以 navy 一开始是一群船，而不是一个机构。

normal.en: Old French navie turned the ship word into a collective, and English kept the shape but changed the ending to y.
normal.cn: 古法语 navie 把「船」这个词变成集合名词，英语保留了这个形状，只把词尾写成 y。

normal.en: Naval is navy plus the Latin adjective ending -al, and it describes anything belonging to a fleet.
normal.cn: naval 是 navy 加上拉丁语形容词词尾 -al，用来形容属于舰队的一切。

normal.en: Navigate is built on the same navis: a ship finding its way is the original picture behind navigation.
normal.cn: navigate 建立在同一个 navis 上：船自己找路，就是 navigation 背后的原初画面。

normal.en: Navy blue is the colour of the cloth, not a shade invented by the service; the uniform gave the dye its English name.
normal.cn: navy blue 是那种布料的颜色，不是海军发明的一种色号；是制服让这种染料有了英语名字。

abstract.en: A word that first counted hulls ends up naming a ministry, a colour and a suit in a shop window.
abstract.cn: 一个原本数船体的词，最后命名了一个部、一种颜色和橱窗里的一套西装。

abstract.en: Uniforms turn a trade into a colour, and a colour into a word that outlives the trade.
abstract.cn: 制服把一种职业变成一种颜色，又让这种颜色变成比职业活得更久的词。

abstract.en: The same stem that names a warship also names the quiet skill of knowing where you are.

definition_en: a person whose job is to type letters or documents

senses.title: The working hands

definition_en: to shake slightly because of cold, fear, or excitement, or such a shaking
core_image: 寒风里一个人缩着肩，牙齿轻轻打颤
scene: 冷风让她发抖。 The cold wind made her shiver.

senses.title: Shake from cold

senses.title: A shaking

definition_en: a vehicle with four wheels, pulled by animals or an engine and used to carry goods
core_image: 两匹马拉着高帮的木车，轮子在土路上碾出两道深印
scene: 集市散场，帮工把菜筐一只只搬上车，车夫扯了扯缰绳，车轮吱吱地压过石板路。 The wagon rolled slowly towards the river with a load of hay.

senses.title: A four-wheeled cart for goods
senses.definition: a strong cart with four wheels, pulled by horses or oxen and used to move goods
senses.definitionCN: 四轮的结实大车，由马或牛牵引运货
senses.example: The wagon rolled slowly towards the river with a load of hay.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆装满干草的马车缓缓朝河边驶去。
senses.why: The word came from Dutch and named the plain working cart of farm and market.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自荷兰语，指农场与集市上用的一般活计车。

senses.title: A railway truck
senses.definition: in British use, an open railway truck for goods rather than passengers
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中指针运货而不载客的敞篷铁路车厢
senses.example: A long line of coal wagons stood waiting in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 调车场里停着一长列等着装煤的车皮。
senses.why: Railways simply moved the old word from the road to the rail, keeping its job of carrying goods.
senses.whyCN: 铁路只是把这个旧词从土路搬到铁轨上，保留它运货的职分。

senses.title: A covered settler vehicle
senses.definition: in American history, the covered wagon that carried families westward
senses.definitionCN: 美国历史中载着家庭向西迁徙的带篷车
senses.example: Their family crossed the plains in a single wagon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一家只靠一辆篷车横穿草原。
senses.why: The same cart, given a canvas cover, became both house and transport for settlers.
senses.whyCN: 同一辆大车加上帆布篷，就成了移民的住所兼交通工具。

senses.title: Part of a compound name
senses.definition: in compound names, a vehicle built on the same frame, as in station wagon or chuck wagon

senses.example: He parked the station wagon outside the diner.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旅行车停在餐车小馆外面。
senses.why: The carrying body of the old cart survives in names of vehicles built to hold things.
senses.whyCN: 旧大车的载货身形，存活在那些为装东西而造的车辆名称里。

senses.title: A figure for giving up
senses.definition: in the phrase fall off the wagon, to return to a bad habit such as drinking
senses.definitionCN: 在 fall off the wagon 中，指重新染上酗酒等恶习
senses.example: He stayed dry for a year and then fell off the wagon.
senses.exampleCN: 他戒了一年，后来又喝上了。
senses.why: The phrase came from temperance speech, where staying on the water wagon meant drinking no alcohol.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法出自戒酒宣传：待在运水车上，就是不喝酒。

intro.en: Wagon came into English from Dutch wagen, a word for a farm cart, in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: wagon 在十六世纪从荷兰语 wagen（农用大车）进入英语。

items.en: Wagen meant a wagon or cart, and Dutch trade and farming brought the word to England.
items.cn: wagen 意为大车，荷兰的贸易与农事把这个词带到了英格兰。

items.en: The Dutch word descends from a Germanic root for a vehicle, related to English way and to wain.
items.cn: 这个荷兰词源自日耳曼语表示车辆的词根，与英语 way、wain 有关。

items.en: English spelt it waggon for centuries, and wagon was later fixed in American use.
items.cn: 英语曾长期拼作 waggon，后来美式用法定下 wagon。

items.en: Railways gave the word a new job for goods trucks, still common in British speech.
items.cn: 铁路给它添了运货车皮的新用法，这一层在英式英语里仍然常见。

items.en: In America the covered wagon became a national image, and the station wagon followed the car.
items.cn: 在美洲，带篷车成了国民意象，汽车时代又有旅行车接续。

note.en: The first group gathers the cart family and spellings, the second the other vehicles of the road and rail.
note.cn: 第一组收大车词族与不同拼法，第二组收路上与铁道上其他的车。

entries.definition: The plural form.
The older British spelling.
The person who drives a wagon.
The road the wagon travels, from the same old root.
A cart usually has only two wheels.
A wheeled vehicle, often for passengers.
A motor goods vehicle, the modern heir of the wagon.
The British word for a large motor truck.

normalIntro.en: Wagon is a borrowed working word, so it is best held by the picture of four wheels and a load.
normalIntro.cn: wagon 是个借来的干活用的词，最好靠「四个轮子加一车货」的画面记住。

normal.en: Four wheels and a load is the whole idea of a wagon.
normal.cn: 四个轮子加一车货，就是 wagon 的全部意思。

normal.en: Wagons carry goods; carriages carry people.
normal.cn: wagon 运货，carriage 载人。

normal.en: British spelling waggon has a double g.
normal.cn: 英式拼法 waggon 是两个 g。

normal.en: A station wagon is the car version, still a carrier.
normal.cn: 旅行车是汽车版本，仍然在载东西。

normal.en: Off the wagon means drinking again, as if stepping off a cart.
normal.cn: off the wagon 指又喝上了，仿佛从车上下来。

abstract.en: See two deep ruts in a wet lane.
abstract.cn: 想湿泥路上两道深辙。

abstract.en: Hear a wooden wheel creak over stone.
abstract.cn: 听木轮在石板上吱吱作响。

abstract.en: Feel a heavy load settle and the cart push forward.
abstract.cn: 感受重货落稳，车往前一推。

examples.en: They loaded the wagon with apples before dawn.
examples.cn: 天亮前他们把苹果装上了马车。

examples.en: A line of wagons waited outside the mill.
examples.cn: 一列车等在磨坊外。

examples.en: The children rode in the back of the wagon.
examples.cn: 孩子们坐在马车后斗里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖根」——车轮太重，把路上的土挖出了两道深根似的辙。

root: 荷兰语 wagen（大车）→ 英语 wagon；更早源自日耳曼语表示车辆的词根，与 way、wain 同源。

sensesIntro.en: One working cart spreads into the railway truck, the settler’s covered wagon, the modern estate car and one old drinker’s idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: 一辆干活的大车，扩展成铁路车皮、移民的篷车、现代的旅行车，以及一句老酒鬼的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four wooden wheels under a load.
core.cn: 核心意象：一车货下的四个木轮。

branches.en: The farm branch: hay going down to the river.
branches.cn: 农事分支：干草车往河边走。

branches.en: The railway branch: coal trucks in the yard.
branches.cn: 铁路分支：调车场里的煤车。

branches.en: The settler branch: one wagon across the plains.
branches.cn: 移民分支：一辆车横穿草原。

branches.en: The car branch: the estate car outside a diner.
branches.cn: 汽车分支：小馆外的旅行车。

branches.en: The idiom branch: sober for a year, then not.
branches.cn: 习语分支：戒了一年，又喝了。

intro.en: Wagon is a whole borrowed word; its parts are old Germanic, and the family grows with -er and the spelling waggon.
intro.cn: wagon 是整词借入，其内部构件属古日耳曼语，词族靠 -er 与拼法 waggon 扩展。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the word is Germanic and came through Dutch, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，属日耳曼语并经由荷兰语传入，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: The root is shared with way.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 way 共用。

items.example: The direct source of the English word.
The Dutch ending stayed in English.
items.exampleCN: 荷兰语词尾留在了英语里。

items.example: Same old root, a different branch.

definition_en: a thick cloud near the ground, a state of confusion, or to cover something with mist
core_image: 清晨的街道被白雾吞没，路灯只剩一圈模糊的光
scene: 浓雾笼罩着整条街。 Thick fog covered the whole street.
sceneCN: 这里 fog 是「雾」（第 1 个义项）；句意：浓雾笼罩着整条街。

senses.title: Ground cloud
senses.definition: a thick cloud of tiny water drops near the ground
senses.definitionCN: 贴近地面的浓密小水滴云团
senses.example: Thick fog covered the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 浓雾笼罩着整条街。
senses.why: This is the basic weather sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的天气义项。

senses.title: Confusion
senses.definition: a state of being unable to think clearly
senses.definitionCN: 无法清晰思考的状态
senses.example: He was in a fog after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后他脑子一片迷雾。
senses.why: Mental cloudiness mirrors real fog.
senses.whyCN: 头脑的迷糊对应真实的雾。

senses.title: To become misty
senses.definition: to cover with mist or steam
senses.definitionCN: 被雾气或水汽覆盖
senses.example: The mirror fogged up in the bathroom.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室的镜子蒙上了水汽。
senses.why: The weather noun turns into a process.
senses.whyCN: 天气名词转为过程。

senses.title: To blur
senses.definition: to make something hard to see clearly
senses.definitionCN: 使某物难以看清
senses.example: Steam fogged the camera lens.
senses.exampleCN: 水汽使相机镜头模糊了。
senses.why: Mist blocks the view of an object.
senses.whyCN: 雾遮挡了对物体的视线。

intro.en: Fog is a word of uncertain origin, perhaps from a northern word for spray.
intro.cn: fog 来源不确定，可能来自北方语言中表示水沫的词。

items.en: The earliest fog may have meant sea spray.
items.cn: 最早的 fog 可能指海上的水沫。

items.en: Related northern words described mist and spray.
items.cn: 相关的北方词语描述雾和飞沫。

items.en: Fog named thick mist near the ground.
items.cn: fog 指贴近地面的浓雾。

items.en: Fog extended to blurred glass and confusion.
items.cn: fog 扩展到模糊的玻璃与困惑。

items.en: Fog up became a common phrasal verb.
items.cn: fog up 成为常用短语动词。

note.en: Fog is compared with similar-looking words and with words for mist.
note.cn: 把 fog 与形近词以及表示薄雾的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small jumping water animal
a wild animal with a bushy tail
to run slowly
thin fog in small drops
light mist in the air
a mass of water drops in the sky

normalIntro.en: Fog is a cloud that has come down to the street.
normalIntro.cn: fog 是降到街道上的云。

normal.en: The fog is thick this morning.
normal.cn: 今天早上雾很浓。

normal.en: The car disappeared into the fog.
normal.cn: 汽车消失在雾中。

normal.en: My glasses fogged up.
normal.cn: 我的眼镜起雾了。

normal.en: He is in a fog about the plan.
normal.cn: 他对这个计划一头雾水。

normal.en: Morning fog often clears by noon.
normal.cn: 晨雾通常在中午前散去。

abstract.en: Fog makes the nearest thing look distant.
abstract.cn: 雾让最近的东西看起来很远。

abstract.en: A confused mind is a room full of fog.
abstract.cn: 困惑的头脑是一间充满雾的房间。

abstract.en: You can walk through fog but not see through it.
abstract.cn: 你可以走过雾，却看不穿它。

examples.en: Thick fog covered the whole street.
examples.cn: 浓雾笼罩着整条街。

examples.en: The mirror fogged up in the bathroom.
examples.cn: 浴室的镜子蒙上了水汽。

examples.en: Steam fogged the camera lens.
examples.cn: 水汽使相机镜头模糊了。

dict_mnemonic.text: fog 是贴地的云：挡住视线，也比喻脑子被迷雾挡住。

root: 中古英语 fogge，来源不确定，核心义「贴近地面的浓密水汽」。

sensesIntro.en: Fog means ground mist, mental confusion, to become misty, or to blur.
sensesIntro.cn: fog 意为雾、困惑、起雾或使模糊。

core.en: A cloud of water drops that hides the view.
core.cn: 遮住视线的水滴云团。

branches.en: Weather that swallows the street.
branches.cn: 吞没街道的天气。

branches.en: A mind that cannot see clearly.
branches.cn: 看不清的头脑。

branches.en: Glass turned white with steam.
branches.cn: 玻璃被水汽变白。

branches.en: A lens that no longer sees.
branches.cn: 不再看清的镜头。

branches.en: Weather and confusion share one image.
branches.cn: 天气与困惑共享同一个意象。

intro.en: Fog forms a small family of mist and clearing words.
intro.cn: fog 形成一个表示雾与除雾的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Fog has no Latin ancestor; Latin nebula, mist, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fog 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 nebula（雾）只是语义对应词。

items.meaningCN: 雾（复数）；起雾（第三人称单数）

items.example: The fogging of the glass spoiled the photo.
Press the button to defog the screen.
The car has a rear defogger.

definition_zh: 线；细丝；线索；思路；螺纹；（网络）帖子
definition_en: a very thin strand of cotton or other fibre, or a connecting line of thought, story or discussion
core_image: 一根极细的线穿过针眼，把散开的布片一点点连起来
scene: 老人补旧棉袄,眯着眼把一根细白的线往针眼里送了三次才穿过去。 She licked the end of the thread and pushed it through the eye of the needle.
sceneCN: 这里 thread 是「线、细丝」（第 1 个义项：缝纫用的极细纤维）；句意为她舔湿线头，把它穿进针眼。

derivatives.zh: thread 与 bare 复合，义为「（布料）磨得起毛露线的；陈腐的」
由本词加 -like 构成，义为「线状的；细如丝的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「穿线；螺纹加工」

senses.title: A thin strand for sewing
senses.definition: a very thin strand of cotton, silk or other fibre, used to sew cloth or weave fabric
senses.definitionCN: 棉、丝或其他纤维制成的极细股线，用于缝布或织布
senses.example: She pulled a red thread through the hem of the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一根红线穿过了窗帘的下摆。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a twisted fibre, spun thin enough to pass through a needle’s eye.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意义是搓成的纤维，细到能穿过针眼。

senses.title: A connecting line of thought
senses.definition: the connecting line that holds an argument, story or explanation together
senses.definitionCN: 把论证、故事或解释串起来的连接线索
senses.example: I lost the thread of his argument halfway through.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲到一半，我就跟不上他的论证思路了。
senses.why: A thread runs invisibly through cloth; an argument has just such a line running through it.
senses.whyCN: 线在布中看不见地延伸；一段论证里也正有这样一条线。

senses.title: A thin line of something
senses.definition: a thin stream or line of liquid, smoke, light or similar
senses.definitionCN: 液体、烟、光等形成的一缕细流
senses.example: A thin thread of smoke rose from the chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 一缕细细的烟从烟囱里升起。
senses.why: Anything stretched thin enough to look like a strand borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 凡是拉得足够细、看起来像股线的东西，都可以借用这个词。

senses.title: A ridge on a screw
senses.definition: the continuous spiral ridge cut around a screw, bolt or pipe
senses.definitionCN: 螺钉、螺栓或管子上连续盘旋的凸棱
senses.example: The thread on this bolt is worn and no longer grips.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗螺栓的螺纹磨损了，已经拧不住。
senses.why: A spiral ridge is literally a thread wound round a cylinder, the image carried into metal.
senses.whyCN: 螺旋凸棱本就是把线绕在圆柱上，这个意象被带进了金属里。

senses.title: A linked online discussion
senses.definition: a series of linked messages on a forum or social platform, replies hanging under one post
senses.definitionCN: 论坛或社交平台上一串相互关联的留言，回复挂在一个帖子下
senses.example: Her question drew a long thread of replies.
senses.exampleCN: 她的问题引来了一长串回复。
senses.why: The digital thread is stitched from messages: each reply is sewn onto the one before.
senses.whyCN: 网络上的串由一条条消息缝成：每个回复都被缝在前一条上。

senses.title: To pass through a narrow space
senses.definition: to move carefully through a narrow space or a crowd, or to pass something through a small opening
senses.definitionCN: 小心地穿过狭窄空间或人群，或把某物穿过小孔
senses.example: We threaded our way through the market crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在市场的人流中穿行而过。
senses.why: The verb keeps the needle image: something thin is pushed through a small gap.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了针的意象：细长之物被推过狭小的缝隙。

intro.en: Thread is a native English word whose root meant to twist; the same root lies behind throw and through.
intro.cn: thread 是英语本土词，词根意为「搓、扭」；同一个词根也藏在 throw 与 through 里。

items.en: The root meant to twist or wind, which describes exactly how fibre is spun into thread.
items.cn: 词根意为「搓、缠」，正是纤维被纺成线的过程。

items.en: Old English þræd meant a fine spun cord, and the verb form already meant to pass through a narrow opening.
items.cn: 古英语 þræd 意为细纺成的线，其动词形式已表示「穿过狭窄处」。

items.en: Middle English used the noun for both sewing fibre and the warp of cloth, and began the figurative sense of a line of speech.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个名词兼指缝线与本布的经线，并开始出现「话里的线」这类比喻。

items.en: By the nineteenth century a thread could be any thin line, from smoke to a mountain path.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，thread 可以指任何细线，从一缕烟到一条山径。

items.en: The digital age added one more: an online thread where replies hang from one message.
items.cn: 数字时代又添一义：回复挂在一条消息下的网络帖子。

note.en: The first group gathers the twisted-root family and near spellings; the second compares thin lines and linked sequences.
note.cn: 第一组收「搓、扭」词根的一族词与形近词；第二组比较细线与相互关联的序列。

entries.definition: Worn so thin that the threads show; also used of tired, stale ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 磨得露线的；也指陈旧乏味的

entries.definition: Thin and long like a thread.
A warning of harm; a near spelling with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 威胁；与 thread 拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: To send something through the air; it shares the twisted, turning root.
entries.definitionCN: 投掷；与 thread 同属「扭、转」词根

entries.definition: A thicker cord, or a series of items on one line.
entries.definitionCN: 细绳；一串（比 thread 粗，且常用于成串之物）

entries.definition: Spun fibre used for knitting, thicker than sewing thread.
entries.definitionCN: 纱；毛线（比缝线粗，用于编织）

entries.definition: A single thin length of hair, rope or fibre.
entries.definitionCN: 一缕；一股（单根细长之物）

entries.definition: A piece of evidence that guides an investigation; it shares the image of a guiding thread.
entries.definitionCN: 线索（与「引路之线」意象相通）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the twisting root, the needle image, and the later figurative senses.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「搓、扭」词根、针线意象，以及后起的比喻义。

normal.en: The root meant to twist, and thread is fibre twisted into a single fine line.
normal.cn: 词根意为「搓」，thread 就是被搓成一根细线的纤维。

normal.en: Thread a needle keeps the physical picture, and threading through a crowd keeps the same narrow gap.
normal.cn: thread a needle 保留实物画面，threading through a crowd 保留同一个窄缝。

normal.en: Lose the thread means the line of an argument has slipped out of your hand.
normal.cn: lose the thread 意为论证的那根线从手中滑走了。

normal.en: A thread of hope is the thinnest possible line of it.
normal.cn: a thread of hope 是希望细到不能再细的一线。

normal.en: An online thread is messages sewn one after another.
normal.cn: 网络 thread 是一条条消息被缝在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a single white thread crossing a dark cloth: the cloth is the topic, the thread is the point.
abstract.cn: 想象一根白线穿过深色布料：布是话题，线才是要点。

abstract.en: Anything long and thin, from smoke to a path, is the same line drawn with another material.
abstract.cn: 凡细长之物，从烟到小径，都是用另一种材料画出的同一条线。

abstract.en: Pull one thread and the whole cloth moves: that is how an idea holds a story together.
abstract.cn: 抽动一根线，整块布都动：这就是一个念头如何撑起一个故事。

examples.en: Use a darker thread so the stitches will not show.
examples.cn: 用深一点的线，这样针脚就不显眼。

examples.en: Try to follow the thread of the story to the end.
examples.cn: 试着顺着故事的线索读到结尾。

examples.en: We threaded through the narrow lanes of the old town.
examples.cn: 我们穿行在老城的窄巷中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思锐的」——思绪锐利得像一根细线，穿过所有乱麻 → thread 线；思路

root: 古英语 þræd，源自日耳曼词根「搓、扭」，本指纺成的细线；同根词还有 throw「投掷」与 through「穿过」。由实物之线引申出思路、细流、螺纹与网络帖子等义。

sensesIntro.en: Thread begins as twisted fibre and then lends its thin connecting line to thought, smoke, screws, crowds and online replies.
sensesIntro.cn: thread 从搓成的纤维开始，再把这根细连接线借给思路、烟缕、螺纹、人群与网络回复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one white thread crossing a dark cloth and holding the pieces together.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根白线穿过深色布料，把布片连在一起。

branches.en: The object: fibre thin enough for a needle.
branches.cn: 实物线：细到能穿针的纤维。

branches.en: The invisible line: through an argument or through the air as smoke.
branches.cn: 无形线：穿过论证，或以烟的形式穿过空气。

branches.en: The metal line: a ridge wound like thread round a bolt.
branches.cn: 金属线：像线一样绕在螺栓上的凸棱。

branches.en: The shared line: replies stitched to one message online.
branches.cn: 共享线：网络上缝在同一条消息上的回复。

branches.en: The action: pushing something thin through a narrow gap.
branches.cn: 动作线：把细长之物推过窄缝。

intro.en: Thread compounds freely with bare and like, and the verb takes ordinary -ing and -ed endings.
intro.cn: thread 能与 bare、like 自由复合，动词则加普通的 -ing 与 -ed。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: from one side to the other

definition_zh: 精心制作的；繁复的；详尽的；详细阐述
definition_en: having many carefully arranged parts, planned in great detail, or to explain something more fully
core_image: 一件木雕上刻满细密的缠枝纹，刀刀不省
scene: 那张桌子的每条腿都雕满缠枝纹，做的人不肯省一刀。 The table has an elaborate carved base.
sceneCN: 这里 elaborate 是「繁复精细的」（第 1 个义项：部件众多且精心安排）；句意是这张桌子的底座雕工繁复。

pos.zh: 形容词：精心制作的；繁复的；详尽的
动词：详细阐述；进一步说明

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

senses.title: Having many carefully made parts
senses.definition: having many parts or details that were made with care, sometimes more than is needed
senses.definitionCN: 部件或细节众多且制作精心，有时多到超出必要
senses.example: The table has an elaborate carved base.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子的底座雕工繁复。
senses.why: Elaborate is Latin elaboratus, worked out; labour is visible in every added part.
senses.whyCN: elaborate 是拉丁语 elaboratus，意为「做出来的」；每多一个部件，都能看见那份劳作。

senses.title: Planned in great detail
senses.definition: worked out with great care and in many steps, as a plan or system
senses.definitionCN: 经过细致推敲、步骤繁多，如计划或体系
senses.example: They worked out an elaborate plan for the escape.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为逃跑制定了一套周密的计划。
senses.why: A plan is also a thing made, so the same word covers the labour of thought rather than of hands.
senses.whyCN: 计划同样是被做出来的东西，于是同一个词也能覆盖头脑的劳作而不只是手上的。

senses.title: To explain more fully
senses.definition: to add more detail to what has been said or written
senses.definitionCN: 为已说或已写的内容补充更多细节
senses.example: Could you elaborate on that last point?
senses.exampleCN: 你能就最后一点详细说明吗？
senses.why: To elaborate is to keep working the material until the shape is complete, so speech is treated like wood.
senses.whyCN: elaborate 就是继续加工材料直到形状完整，于是言语也被当成木头来雕。

intro.en: Elaborate comes from Latin elaboratus, the past participle of elaborare, to labour out, from e- out plus laborare, to work.
intro.cn: elaborate 来自拉丁语 elaboratus，即 elaborare（费力做出）的过去分词，由 e-（出）加 laborare（劳作）构成。

items.en: Labor meant toil or effort, the noun behind the verb.
items.cn: labor 意为「辛劳、费力」，是动词背后的名词。

items.en: The verb meant to work, to toil or to be in difficulty.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「劳作、辛苦、处于困难」。

items.en: E- out plus laborare formed the verb to work out or take pains over.
items.cn: e-（出）加 laborare 构成「做出来、为之费力」的动词。

items.en: The participle described something worked out with care, hence finely made.
items.cn: 分词描述经过仔细加工而成的东西，因此是「精细制作的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective for ornamented things and later formed a verb from it.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词指装饰繁复之物，后来又由它造出动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elaboration family; the near-meaning group separates intricate, detailed and ornate.
note.cn: 形近组收 elaboration 词族；近义组区分 intricate、detailed 与 ornate。

entries.definition: The act of explaining in more detail, or of working something out fully.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「详述；精心制作」，由 elaborate 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: In a detailed or heavily ornamented manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「繁复地；精心地」。

entries.definition: Work, especially hard physical work; the root of elaborate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「劳动」，是本词的词根来源。

entries.definition: Having many small parts arranged in a way that is hard to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「错综复杂的」，强调难以看清的结构。

entries.definition: Containing many facts or small points, without the sense of ornament.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「详细的」，只有细节多，不含装饰义。

entries.definition: Richly decorated; it stresses decoration rather than planning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「华丽装饰的」，强调装饰而非谋划。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a carving knife, then move to a plan on paper and finally to a speaker adding detail.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一把刻刀出发，再走到纸上的计划，最后落到补充细节的说话人。

normal.en: Elaborate carries labour in it: every extra part cost work.
normal.cn: elaborate 里藏着 labour：每多一个部件都是劳作。

normal.en: A carved table leg is elaborate; a plain one is not.
normal.cn: 雕花的桌腿是 elaborate，光的就不是。

normal.en: A plan can be as elaborate as a carving.
normal.cn: 一份计划可以和一件雕刻一样繁复。

normal.en: To elaborate on a point is to keep carving it.
normal.cn: elaborate on 一点，就是继续雕那一点。

normal.en: Elaborate is the adjective; elaborate is also the verb, same spelling.
normal.cn: elaborate 既是形容词也是动词，拼写相同。

abstract.en: Picture a woodcarver who refuses to leave a surface plain.
abstract.cn: 想象一位不肯让任何平面空着的木雕师。

abstract.en: The same patience can go into a table, a plan, or an answer.
abstract.cn: 同一份耐性可以用在桌子、计划或一个回答上。

abstract.en: Elaborate means the work has been worked again and again.
abstract.cn: elaborate 意味着这件东西被一遍遍加工过。

examples.en: The table has an elaborate carved base.
examples.cn: 这张桌子的底座雕工繁复。

examples.en: They worked out an elaborate plan for the escape.
examples.cn: 他们为逃跑制定了一套周密的计划。

examples.en: Could you elaborate on that last point?
examples.cn: 你能就最后一点详细说明吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊拉伯瑞特」——桌腿刻满缠枝纹，一刀也不肯省

root: 拉丁语 laborare「劳作」加前缀 e-「出」构成 elaborare「费力做出」，其过去分词 elaboratus 意为「精心做成的」，英语借入为形容词，后又用作动词「详述」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elaborate: richly made, carefully planned in detail, and the verb meaning to explain more fully.
sensesIntro.cn: elaborate 的三个义项：制作繁复、谋划周密，以及动词「详细阐述」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved table leg covered in dense vine patterns, no cut spared.
core.cn: 核心意象：雕满细密缠枝纹的桌腿，一刀也不省。

branches.en: THE CARVING: many parts, each one worked by hand.
branches.cn: 雕工线：部件众多，每一件都手工加工。

branches.en: THE PLAN: the same patience spent on thought instead of wood.
branches.cn: 计划线：同一份耐性用在思虑而非木头上。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION: the speaker keeps working the point.
branches.cn: 说明线：说话人继续加工那一点。

branches.en: THE DETAIL: whether hands or head, the detail is deliberate.
branches.cn: 细节线：无论用手还是用脑，细节都是有意加的。

branches.en: THE UNFOLDING: a detailed plan and a detailed answer both open outward.
branches.cn: 展开线：周密的计划与详尽的回答都向外铺开。

intro.en: Elaborate is e- plus the Latin labour verb; English then adds -ion, -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: elaborate 是 e- 加拉丁语「劳作」动词；英语随后再加 -ion、-ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor, laborare and elaboratus are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 labor、laborare 与 elaboratus 均有记录，只有更深的印欧词根属于重构。

items.exampleCN: 它与 laborare 构成 elaborare。

definition_zh: 外面的；外部的；外围的；远离中心的；表面的
definition_en: on or near the outside of something; farther from the centre than another part; and also describing what is shown rather than felt inside
core_image: 两只叠在一起的碗，手先摸到最外那一圈，凉得更快
scene: 冬天的早上，两只叠着的碗放在窗台上，手碰到最外面那一圈，凉得更快。 The outer layer of paint had begun to peel.
sceneCN: 这里是「外面的、外部的」（第 1 个义项：最靠外的一层）；句意为最外面那层漆已经开始脱落。图中可辨识物件：叠着的碗、窗台、剥落的漆面。

pos.zh: 外面的；外部的；外围的；远离中心的；表面的

derivatives.zh: 由 outer 加最高级后缀 -most 构成，义为「最外面的；离中心最远的」
由 outer 与 wear 复合而成，义为「外衣；外套类服装」
由 out 加方向后缀 -ward 构成，义为「向外的；外表的」，与 outer 侧重位置不同

senses.title: On the outside of something
senses.definition: on or near the outside of a thing, especially of a layer that covers or surrounds something else
senses.definitionCN: 在一件东西的外面或靠近外面，尤指覆盖、包围另一物的那一层
senses.example: A thin outer shell protects the seed.
senses.exampleCN: 一层薄薄的外壳保护着种子。
senses.why: Outer is the comparative of out, so it marks the side that is more out than the other, which is why it usually names the covering layer when two layers are compared.
senses.whyCN: outer 是 out 的比较级，标出两者中「更靠外」的那一边，所以当两层东西相比时，它通常指起覆盖作用的那一层。

senses.title: Farther from the centre
senses.definition: situated at a greater distance from the centre, as in the outer ring of a city or the outer planets
senses.definitionCN: 离中心更远的位置，如城市的外环或外侧的行星
senses.example: They moved from the crowded centre to an outer suburb.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从拥挤的市中心搬到一处外围郊区。
senses.why: Because the comparative points away from a middle, the word also measures distance from a centre, so a city or a solar system can be split into inner and outer zones.
senses.whyCN: 既然比较级指的是背离中心的方向，这个词也用来量离中心的距离，于是一座城市或一个星系都能分成内圈与外圈。

senses.title: Shown rather than felt
senses.definition: belonging to the surface of a person or thing, as opposed to what is hidden or felt inside
senses.definitionCN: 属于人或物的表层，与藏在里面、真实感到的东西相对
senses.example: Beneath his outer calm, he was badly shaken.
senses.exampleCN: 他表面镇定，内心却受到很大震动。
senses.why: If outer names the layer people can see, then a person's composure can be spoken of as an outer layer, with the hidden feeling lying behind it.
senses.whyCN: 如果 outer 指的正是别人看得见的那一层，那么一个人的镇定也可以说成一层外皮，藏起来的情绪就在它后面。

intro.en: Outer is an English comparative of out, formed by adding -er to the adverb; it is generally taken to have replaced an older comparative that survives in utter.
intro.cn: outer 是英语用副词 out 加 -er 构成的比较级；一般认为它取代了一个更老的比较级，那个形式留在 utter 里。

items.en: The reconstructed root behind out meant outward, and it supplied the adverb in several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ūt 意为向外，在几种日耳曼语里都提供了这个副词。

items.en: Old English ūt meant out, and its comparative ūtera named what is more out or farther out; that form survives in utter.
items.cn: 古英语 ūt 意为在外、向外，它的比较级 ūtera 指更靠外的东西；这个形式后来留在 utter 里。

items.en: Middle English added -er to out again and produced outer, generally read as a newer doublet of the older comparative.
items.cn: 中古英语又给 out 加了一次 -er，造出 outer，一般认为它是那个更老比较级的新替身。

items.en: English fixed outer as the adjective for the outside member of a pair or set, especially in outer wall, outer ring and outer room.
items.cn: 英语把 outer 固定为形容词，指一对或一组事物里靠外的那一个，尤其用于外墙、外环、外间。

items.en: Modern English extends it to space and cities, giving outer space, outer suburbs and the superlative outermost.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到太空与城市，产生 outer space、outer suburbs 以及最高级 outermost。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the out family and its older comparative; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what lies on or beyond a surface.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 out 词族及其更老比较级展开；近义组收表示「位于表面或表面之外」的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb and preposition from which outer was formed by adding a comparative ending.
entries.definitionCN: outer 由它加比较级词尾构成，意为向外、在外。

entries.definition: Farthest out, or farthest from the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 最外面的；离中心最远的。

entries.definition: An older comparative of out, now mainly meaning complete or absolute.
entries.definitionCN: out 更老的比较级，现在主要表示「完全的、彻底的」。

entries.definition: Going or pointing away from the inside.
Coming from or belonging to the outside.
The outside surface of a building or object.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物或物体的外表面。

entries.definition: On the edge or outer boundary of something.
The flat top or outside layer of a thing.

normalIntro.en: Outer is a comparative of out, so the mnemonics compare two positions and always pick the one farther from the middle.
normalIntro.cn: outer 是 out 的比较级，所以联想始终在比较两个位置，并且总挑离中间更远的那个。

normal.en: Outer is out plus the comparative ending -er, so it literally says more out.
normal.cn: outer 是 out 加比较级词尾 -er，字面就是「更靠外」。

normal.en: Old English had a comparative ūtera, and that older form survives in utter.
normal.cn: 古英语本来就有比较级 ūtera，这个更老的形式留在 utter 里。

normal.en: Outermost adds -most and pushes the comparison to the extreme.
normal.cn: outermost 加 -most，把比较推到最尽头。

normal.en: Outerwear is outer plus wear: the clothing worn as the outside layer.
normal.cn: outerwear 是 outer 加 wear：当作最外层穿的衣服。

normal.en: Outward uses -ward, which marks direction, while outer marks position.
normal.cn: outward 用 -ward 标方向，而 outer 标位置。

abstract.en: Two bowls stacked, and the hand reaching for the cooler rim.
abstract.cn: 两只碗叠着，手先摸到更凉的那一圈外沿。

abstract.en: A city drawn as two rings: the word only makes sense when there is a middle to be far from.
abstract.cn: 把城市画成两个圈：这个词只有在存在一个可供远离的中心时才成立。

abstract.en: A calm face with something behind it: the outside layer is also a screen.
abstract.cn: 一张平静的脸背后藏着东西：外层同时也是一道屏风。

examples.cn: 一层薄薄的外壳保护着种子。

examples.en: They moved from the crowded centre to an outer suburb.
examples.cn: 他们从拥挤的市中心搬到一处外围郊区。

examples.en: Beneath his outer calm, he was badly shaken.
examples.cn: 他表面镇定，内心却受到很大震动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凹特」——两只碗叠着，手总先摸到外面那一圈；记住 outer 是外面的。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a comparison of two positions; the senses go from the covering layer, to distance from a centre, to the face a person shows.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「两个位置的比较」；义项从覆盖的那一层，到离中心的距离，再到一个人露出的表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two stacked bowls, the outer rim wider and cooler to the touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只叠在一起的碗，外沿更宽，摸上去也更凉。

branches.en: a hand testing the cooler rim of a bowl
branches.cn: 一只手试探碗沿更凉的那一圈

branches.en: paint flaking from the outer wall of a house
branches.cn: 房屋外墙剥落的漆

branches.en: a ring road drawn around a crowded centre
branches.cn: 拥挤市中心外围画出的环线

branches.en: a telescope pointed at the outer planets
branches.cn: 望远镜对准外侧的行星

branches.en: a calm face with a clenched hand out of sight
branches.cn: 平静的脸与藏起来的握紧的手
